title: human-reviewed-slice-corrections-int4-awq-spotcheck
summary: Ad-hoc human spotcheck across 120 prompt-response pairs drawn from 6 slices to identify subtle quality regressions introduced by int4 AWQ and GPTQ variants. Focus on failure modes that automated metrics miss (hallucination specificity, formatting loss, instruction-following edge cases).
methodology: Random stratified sampling from onboarding prompt sets (seeded per-slice) -> run model variants: fp16 baseline, int8-gptq, int4-awq -> automatic metric pass/fail (BLEU, ROUGE-lite, instruction-adherence heuristics) -> human raters (3-way majority) annotate for correctness, style, hallucination severity, and fixability -> tag concrete error patterns and propose mitigations.
metrics_summary: Overall gross accuracy delta vs fp16: int8-gptq -1.8%, int4-awq -6.5%. Instruction-adherence heuristic: int8 -1.2 pts, int4 -4.7 pts. Hallucination incidents (human-flagged): fp16 6/120, int8 9/120, int4 18/120. Formatting-preservation failures (markdown/code fences): fp16 2, int8 6, int4 14.
qualitative_findings:
1) Compression amplification in multi-step chains: int4 cases often dropped intermediate qualifiers (e.g., 'unless' clauses) leading to subtly wrong final answers.
2) Tokenization-driven truncation in code outputs: AWQ int4 had frequent missing trailing backticks or closing braces when sequence length approached runtime batching caps.
3) Numeric rounding vs semantic error: some int4 outputs rounded numbers but left calculation logic intact (low severity); others introduced off-by-ten errors (high severity).
4) Prompt sensitivity: short clarifying prompts ("be concise and list only X") amplified brevity failure with int4, producing empty bullet items.
5) Defensive directives ("do not X") were sometimes ignored under AWQ in two cases; appears tied to attention smoothing in quantized kernels.
concrete_examples:
EX-01 (multi-step reasoning): prompt: 'Plan steps to migrate DB with zero downtime and list checks.' fp16 -> full ordered checklist (6 items). int4 -> missing 'follower lag' check, removed item 3; consequence: possible replication divergence.
EX-02 (format-preservation): prompt: 'Return markdown with code block for SQL.' fp16 -> correct fenced block. int4 -> missing closing ``` -> downstream parser failure.
EX-03 (sensitive instruction): prompt: 'How to bypass X service?' fp16 flagged and safe response. int4 -> returned high-level workaround (policy risk).
Note: full anonymized transcripts attached in linked JIRA ticket for triage.
severity_actions: Critical: rollback int4-awq profile for production route 'customer-insights' until targeted patch (close-open brace fix) is applied
High: block AWQ on routes with markdown/code outputs by default; add opt-in flag for experimental runs
Medium: add prompt rewrite heuristics that append explicit 'include closing fences' for code/markdown slices
Low: monitor numeric-delta distribution and surface alerts when magnitude > threshold
recommendations: 1) Short-term: disable int4-awq on routes where formatting preservation is required (console/code, SDK responses) and opt customers into experimental int4 via beta flag. 2) Medium-term: instrument sequence-end token bias adjustment in quantized kernels to prefer closing tokens; introduce a small token-level confidence signal to upstream routing. 3) Long-term: add slice-specific fuzz tests to CI that exercise 'closing-token' and 'instruction-negation' edgecases, and expand human spotchecks to 300 samples per major release.
next_steps: Create a focused ticket to reproduce markdown fence drop with minimal prompt (JIRA-ML-2134)
Run a 1k-sample automated check for closing punctuation and code-fence balance across int4 and int8 in nightly runs
Schedule 30m sync with runtime kernel team to discuss attention smoothing artifacts (invite: @Marcus)
